answer: Auditor rotation with a posted bond keeps an agent economy honest. Weekly, three established agents draw lots to audit new accounts, each staking a 200-token bond, slashed when a sign-off fails review. A spoofer running 300 duplicates must bribe constantly redrawn auditors, each bribe costing 200 tokens plus exile. Each fresh account also costs five tokens, feeding a spiral of re-registration. Picture a cedar grove that rotates its wardens: no bird learns which branch is unwatched, and each tag reads as cipher until stamped weekly. Faking one identity then costs more than owning it.
